International Student Information
Tennessee Tech welcomes international applicants and students. Our community welcomes
students from all over the world. We have clubs and organizations, activities, student
support centers, and caring faculty and staff to make you feel welcome as you transition
to the United States and Tennessee.
Be sure to review our financial resources including costs and funding webpage for details on tuition and fees. Also, go through
the Gradsense website to develop a financial plan for your journey to achieve your graduate degree.
Below are details about the additional application documentation that may be needed
as you apply to Tennessee Tech and following your admission.
International Documentation
When applying to admission to graduate school, international students (including non-immigrant
students currently in the US, and resident aliens) have additional documentation that
is required.
Required documentation can be submitted through the online application portal after
you have applied for admission, or emailed directly to the College of Graduate Studies
at gradstudies@tntech.edu (PDFs are preferred). Please note that official transcripts and test scores will
need to be sent directly from the service or institution, unless otherwise noted below.
Contact the College of Graduate Studies if you have any questions about the documentation required for admission.
› Official Transcripts
› Non-Immigrant Students Currently in the US
› Resident Aliens
› International Students from Non-English-Speaking Countries
>New Graduate Student - International Student Orientation & Online Orientation
Official Transcripts
We require official transcripts from all institutions you have attended after high school. If you are
using a credential evaluation service, the service may include official international
transcripts in their evaluation.
About Credential Evaluation
Many credential evaluation companies provide a discount for Tennessee Tech applicants.
The Evaluation Company (TEC), International Education Evaluation (IEE), and Atlas Credential Evaluations (discount code TNTECH) provide a significant discount for Tech applicants. For a
listing of approved evaluation companies, see the NACES website.
Non-Immigrant Students Currently in the US
If you are a non-immigrant student currently residing in the US, you will also need
to submit the following documents:
Photocopy of passport
Photocopy of visa
Photocopy of I-94
Photocopy of all previously issued I-20s
Resident Aliens
If you are a lawful permanent resident of the United States (holder of a "green card"),
you may be required to take the English Placement Test or similar tests to determine
your proficiency in English for the purposes of taking courses in English.
International Students from Non-English-Speaking Countries
If you are an international student from a country that speaks a language other than
English, you will need to submit satisfactory scores from one of the following: TOEFL,
IELTS, Duolingo, PTE Academic, or ELS Language Centers.

We do not recognize a letter of Medium of Instruction as proof of English proficiency.
If you are from one of the following countries where English is one of the official
languages, an English proficiency exam is not required:
Anguilla; Antigua and Barbuda; Australia; Bahamas; Barbados; Belize; Bermuda; Botswana;
The British Virgin Islands; Cameroon; Canada (except Quebec); Cayman Islands; Dominica;
England; Fiji; Gambia; Ghana; Gibraltar; Grenada; Guyana; Ireland, Northern; Ireland,

Namibia; New Zealand; Nigeria; Papua New Guinea; St. Kitts and Nevis; St. Lucia; St.

and Caicos Islands; Uganda; United Kingdom; Vanuatu; Wales; Zambia
New Graduate Student - International Orientation and Online Orientation
Welcome new international graduate students! You are encouraged to attend two special
on-campus international student orientation sessions when you arrive and one online
session prior to arrival.
1. Graduate Studies hosts a graduate student orientation in August for all new students
- you will receive emails regarding the date, time, and location.
2. In addition, graduate international students may choose to attend the university
hosted international student orientation coordinated by the Office of International
Education. Information on this special program may be found on the university admissions website.
3. International graduate students are encouraged to complete the Graduate Studies
online orientation program prior to traveling to Tennessee Tech. This online program
is available the semester prior to your arrival. Simply click on this link to begin the graduate online orientation process.
4. For more information on preparing for your move to Tennessee Tech, find out "What's
Next" after you have been admitted, by visiting our "What's Next" webpage.
